title: Reading Practice 4 - Coral Reef Ecosystems
description: IELTS Academic Reading practice about coral reef conservation and marine biodiversity.

stimuli.title: Passage 1: Coral Reef Ecosystems
stimuli.content:
A Coral reefs, often called the rainforests of the sea, are among the most biodiverse ecosystems on Earth. Despite covering less than 1% of the ocean floor, they support approximately 25% of all marine species. These remarkable structures are built by tiny animals called coral polyps, which secrete calcium carbonate to form hard skeletons. Over thousands of years, these skeletons accumulate to create the massive reef structures we see today.

B The health of coral reefs is intimately connected to water temperature. Corals live in a symbiotic relationship with microscopic algae called zooxanthellae, which live within the coral tissues and provide them with up to 90% of their energy through photosynthesis. When water temperatures rise even 1-2 degrees Celsius above the normal maximum, corals expel these algae in a process known as coral bleaching. Without their algal partners, the corals turn white and, if conditions do not improve within weeks, they starve and die.

C Human activities pose numerous threats to coral reefs beyond climate change. Overfishing disrupts the delicate balance of reef ecosystems, while destructive fishing practices such as dynamite fishing physically destroy reef structures. Agricultural runoff carries sediment, pesticides, and fertilizers into coastal waters, smothering corals and promoting harmful algal blooms. Coastal development and dredging further degrade reef habitats.

D Conservation efforts are underway around the world to protect remaining coral reefs. Marine Protected Areas have been established in many countries, restricting fishing and other destructive activities. Scientists are also experimenting with coral gardening, growing fragments of resilient coral species in underwater nurseries and transplanting them onto degraded reefs. Some researchers are even exploring genetic modification to create heat-resistant coral strains.
